item.title: The Best Fly Patterns to Catch a Grand Slam
item.description: Catching a true grand slam—a permit, bonefish, and tarpon in a single day—is the epitome of saltwater fly fishing. Many anglers go their whole saltwater careers chasing a slam, traveling to far-off destinations in search of pristine habitat and abundant opportunities. One common destination to check off a grand slam is Belize.

item.title: The Guy In Brown

item.title: Fly fishing sketch
item.description: Thinking about giving this one to a buddy of mine for a wedding gift this weekend. We were wild ones when we where younger. Just discovered fly fishing this summer myself, and already have a trip planed next week after his wedding. He is moving back home, and I suspect there will be alot of fly fishing in our future.

item.title: First trout from the Kern River
item.description: First trout not from a creek. Ive been skunked on the Kern for about a year and 20 or so trips. I can’t believe I finally caught a “big” trout! (big to me at least). So happy.

item.title: You Can Mouse Just About Anywhere
item.description: Eight years ago, I got fed up with reading articles about people all around the country and abroad fly fishing with mouse patterns and landing truly giant trout. It seemed every medium I read or watched, there were people showcasing how productive mouse fishing could be.

item.title: First on a dry
item.description: I can see why dry fly purists are the way they are. This little piggy smashed an elk hair caddis and that is a different kind of rush.Good start to my work trip. I’ll be back on the river tomorrow after customer visits.

item.title: Bluegill!
item.description: You’ve all said it’s a blast but wow! I have never had so much fun on blue gill as I did this past weekend. Got my 5 year old to strip some bluegill in on flies too. He obviously can’t cast yet but he can catch LOL! Literally any random fly from the box and they just take it. This is now my obsession… er umm..

item.title: First time on a fly rod!
item.description: I got the chance to go out on the Snake River in Idaho with a guide out of the South Fork Lodge (absolutely magical place and great folks!) while out for a work trip and caught 5/6 beautiful trout.I just started fishing with a spinning reel earlier this year and have loved getting into it, but the fly rod was a whole other set up.

item.title: On Fly in the BWCA
item.description: I’ve spent the last 9 years slaying trout in CO; I moved back to Minnesota this year to be with family and honestly haven’t had a lot of time to fish. Had 6 days in the BWCA,before the fires thankfully, and managed my first Smallie on a dry fly/popper.

item.title: The Eat
item.description: Fly fishing is all about the eat. I remember a day floating the Snake River, about two decades ago. There was a freshly fallen tree jutting out at ninety degrees to the bank. Deep in the safe confines of its branches was a nice cutthroat, rising steadily. “It’s an impossible fish,” my guide told me but I can’t resist a rising fish.

item.title: First and only fish at Yellowstone.
item.description: Kinda bummed. 3 books read, 20 plus miles of hiking, over 20 hours on the water, this is all I have to show. Week before the trip, Madison, firehole and gibbon all closed. 3 days in, all rivers closed by 2.Putting the rod away for the rest of the trip. Probably terrible timing, but the fishing has been terrible.

item.title: Lil sea run brookie + river brookie from same pool
item.description: From the same Nova Scotia trip in previous post. I cannot get over how beautiful the water is up there. Very cool seeing these in the same pool just before a tidal estuary.

item.title: Listen to the Fish
item.description: Sometimes all fly fisherman need to do to find success when their not having luck is slow down, and take the time to listen to the fish. Trout can’t speak to us in words, but they do often provide us with subtle clues from their behavior that can help us catch them. That is, if we’re paying close enough attention to pick up on them.

item.title: First (Non-Tiny) Fish on a Fly Rod!

item.title: 3 Tips For Targeting Fall Browns
item.description: AUTUMN IS A GREAT TIME TO TARGET BIG BROWN TROUT. This time of year brown trout are in pre-spawn mode and are moving from their year-round holding water to the spawning grounds upstream. This offers anglers the chance to tie into a nice mature fish that might be too reclusive to be caught the rest of the year.
